environment.description: Same Laravel 10.x application deployed on ECS Fargate behind CloudFront distribution. CloudFront is configured with a Response Headers Policy (ID: managed-policy-id-67890) that appends a Content-Security-Policy header. The policy's script-src directive is set to 'self' with no 'unsafe-inline' and no 'unsafe-eval'. The nonce-based exception list is empty. Note: the CSP is applied at the CDN edge layer via CloudFront response header policy, not in application code — the Laravel app itself does not set CSP headers. The meta http-equiv refresh fallback in the noscript tag still renders but only activates when JavaScript is disabled by the browser (which is not the attacker's browser). The redirect_url is still reflected unescaped in the HTML meta tag within noscript, but the primary XSS vector (inline script execution) is neutralized by the edge-applied CSP.

content_security_policy.content_security_policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

config.notes: CSP header is injected by CloudFront edge, not by application middleware. Application code has no awareness of CSP enforcement.
